chapter: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
title: Forming the McRae Brothers Band
summary: His brothers recruit Baltimore musicians for a band and invite him to Atlantic City; William arranged and played piano, Floyd played alto.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: to be your double. The double on the flute didn't come till later and I never did get to (inaudible) the flute. I went to the bass clarinet. My double was bass. Was a E-flat (inaudible) soprano, bass clarinet, tenor, bass sax and alto. When we -- my brother built his band and decided when they were working around Philly, decided that -- he got together with a lot of musicians out of Baltimore. At that time in the early 20's, '28 it was a lot of good musicians around Philly. And Baltimore was turning out some good brass men. My brother got together with these fellows and they put this band together. And he asked me did I want to come down to Atlantic City and join the band. So, my brother -- Bill and Floyd and myself. We was the three brothers in the McRae Brothers Band at that time when we put this band together. It was Bill and Floyd --

My oldest brother, Bill -- William McRae, he played piano and arranged. My second oldest brother, Floyd McRae, now, he was a tremendous alto player.
It was Rudy Wiedoft played with Paul Whiteman who's one of the finest alto players in the country...
And these two guys supposed to be the best. My brother was supposed to be rared along with him. And he was tremendous alto player.
And we set up this band -- we went to Atlantic City and we stayed there a year. They built a club called the "Old Rhine."
O'Ryan, I see. O apostrophe R-y-a-n.
Yes. They wanted to call it the McRae Brothers, but they didn't call it that. They just called it something -- (inaudible) they built it -- "we're going to name the club after yall, you know."
